subjects.name: The 'little Nazis' (ordinary German supporters of Nazism)

summary: How ordinary Germans such as clerks, bakers, teachers and police officers voted for, joined and served the Nazi regime from the 1930s to 1945, enabling the Holocaust through indifference, self-interest and obedience.

evidence.note: focus defined as rank-and-file Nazi supporters, framed through Mayer's postwar book
brief biography of Milton Mayer, born Chicago 1908
long segment on Horst Wessel, his 1930 killing and Goebbels turning him into a martyr
Princeton voting study: self-employed and small owners, not the unemployed, backed the Nazis
1919 communist uprising in Berlin and Freikorps as precursors of the SA
Gellately study of Nazi-era press coverage of camps from 1933 on
Mattner's unit shoots over two thousand Jews at Mogilev, Belarus, in October 1941
Major Trapp's police battalion massacre in occupied Poland, 1942
regular police merged with SS as racial enforcers; Snyder's Black Earth
Mayer's postwar interviews with a chemical engineer who took the 1935 oath

notes: Primary subject is an unnamed mass of ordinary supporters; tagged movement-or-ideology because group requires named people, so roles are empty. Long modern comparisons (Trump, Proud Boys, Patriot Prayer, ICE) justify fascism-far-right but not US in setting. Covered span ends with Mayer's early-1950s interviews (book 1955). Mattner's birth/death years not given, so floruit 1941.
